summary: Discovery call focused on p95 latency targets and token/sec throughput for real-time streaming use cases. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment modes and needs concrete benchmarks with their traces. Key concerns: p95 under burst, concurrency, KV cache behavior, encryption/KMS, and SSO for controls.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
next steps: benchmark run and docs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12 16:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Maya (Ironclad - Head of ML), Tom (Platform Eng), Aisha (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen may be imperfect): Discussed p95 SLA for streaming responses, goal is sub-300ms p95 for short completions (<=128 tokens) at 150 concurrent streams, and steady-state throughput of ~4k tokens/sec for reranking workload. Customer wants Hosted for fast onboarding but needs Dedicated for predictable burst windows during sale events.

--- Transcript body (imperfect auto transcription, timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, good to see you, quick roll call?
[00:12] Maya: Hey Samir, Maya here, Tom and Aisha on from infra side.
[00:16] Tom: yep, Tom.
[00:18] Aisha: Aisha, thanks.
[00:22] Leah: Leah from Redwood, I'll be the SE on this thread, hi all.
[00:28] Ravi: Ravi here, we'll help with benchmarks.
[00:31] Samir: Awesome. High level - Ironclad is evaluating running the recommender/assist features for checkout, so latency matters for conversions, right? Can you share the SLAs you care about?
[00:45] Maya: Yeah we targeted a p95 of around 300ms for streaming prompts under 128 tokens. For some longer generative flows where the assistant writes copy, p95 can be 800ms to 1s is acceptable but we'd prefer lower. Biggest pain though is sales-burst during promo windows - concurrency spikes of 200-300 simultaneous users for 30-45 minutes.
[01:10] Tom: to add, our current on-prem inference pipeline is 1) tokenized request 2) quick rerank then streamed response, we measured peak token/sec about 4k when scaled horizontally. We want to know if Redwood hosted can match or if we need Dedicated.
[01:29] Leah: got it. couple threads to separate: steady-state throughput and burst topology. For streaming, p95 is influenced by batching, KV cache hits, and continuous streaming overhead. With Redwood Dedicated you can set reserved GPU pools to absorb spikes; Hosted can do burst but it's autoscaled so tail latency can vary.
[01:55] Maya: when you say KV cache, can you clarify? we've got sessions that reuse context so cache hit rates are high - would that materially change token/sec?
[02:06] Ravi: yes - if you hit the KV cache or prefix cache we avoid recomputing early layers and only do incremental tokens, that reduces per-token cost and latency. For streaming p95 under cache-hit heavy workloads you can expect 30-60% lower latency versus cold tokens.
[02:30] Aisha: are there quantization tradeoffs we should be aware of? we want high quality for marketing copy.
[02:36] Leah: good question - quantization introduces small nits in quality; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per-model and per-workload. For customer-critical copy we recommend full fp16 for Hosted Dedicated shared pools, and conservatively 4-bit quant for embeddings/rerank to save cost. We'll run evals on your prompt set.
[02:58] Tom: ok great. how do you benchmark p95 for streaming specifically - common tools?
[03:05] Ravi: we usually use a harness that replays real request traces with sequence length distribution. For streaming we instrument token emit timing to measure token-level p95 and end-to-end response p95. We'll provide a script that uses your traces and can run against Hosted and Dedicated endpoints.
[03:28] Maya: timeline wise, we want numbers before Feb 10 internal review. Can you commit to a run and deliver?
[03:35] Samir: yes we can target a benchmark week of Jan 25 as a run, deliver results and a short deck by Feb 5.
[03:42] Maya: perfect.
[03:45] Leah: two more architecture clarifiers - where are your users regionally? that affects region routing and cold-starts.
[03:51] Tom: mostly US east and EU west, small APAC. We prefer data residency kept in US/EU depending on customer locale.
[04:01] Aisha: and we have strict key management - KMS for secrets and SSO via SAML. SOC2 is table stakes.
[04:08] Leah: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private, and hosted has KMS options plus audit logs. We have SOC2 and can share our attestations. For SSO we integrate with SAML/SCIM for RBAC.
[04:25] Maya: are there multi-tenant concerns on Hosted - e.g., noisy neighbour impacting p95?
[04:31] Ravi: Hosted can surface transient tail effects more than Dedicated since Dedicated reserves capacity. We also offer routing policies and automatic fallback to smaller model variants if capacity is constrained. But we should quantify that for your workload.
[04:48] Tom: about numbers, our baseline today: p95 cold 1.2s for 128 tokens, warm sessions 380ms, token/sec steady 4k, concurrency 150 steady, 250 peak during promos. Can Redwood meet warm p95 ~300ms at 150 concurrency?
[05:09] Leah: with Dedicated and prefix caching we usually see warm p95 of ~200-350ms for 128-token flows on the model family you're using (open-family); Hosted warm p95 is often within 10-20% but tail spikes during extreme burst. We'll put exact numbers after we run your traces.
[05:28] Maya: how about streaming fairness when you have 200 short streams - token emission spacing matters for UX.
[05:35] Ravi: yes, we measure token emission jitter. Redwood streaming uses a continuous token path and we can throttle to maintain P95. We'll show plots of token inter-arrival for the run.
[05:52] Samir: one common ask is cost - what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated for your projected QPS?
[05:59] Leah: high level, Hosted is usage-based and good for ramping. Dedicated has a commit (reserved GPUs) but unit cost per token decreases and tail latency predictable. We'll prepare a side-by-side based on your token estimates and burst windows.
[06:15] Tom: for Dedicated - do we get full network isolation? we need private VPC peering and no egress outside our tenancy.
[06:23] Leah: Dedicated offers VPC peering and stricter isolation; Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) gives you still more control with customer-managed control plane. For PCI-sensitive flows, customers often require Private.
[06:37] Aisha: how do you handle canaries and rollbacks for model updates? we can't risk regressions during promotions.
[06:44] Ravi: Redwood Console supports staged rollouts, canary traffic split and automatic fallback to previous model if quality/regression triggers fire. We can tie regression alerts to your eval prompts.
[06:58] Maya: who from Redwood will own the benchmark run and what will you need from us?
[07:03] Samir: Leah and Ravi will run the bench, I'll coordinate and manage pricing follow-up. We need your traces (redacted ok), p95 targets per flow, and any region constraints.
[07:16] Maya: we'll share logs and anonymized request traces by Monday.
[07:20] Samir: perfect.
[07:23] Leah: quick dip into tech: what model family are you testing?
[07:27] Tom: using a tuned open family - quantized 4-bit in production on prem currently, but we have a higher quality fp16 version for marketing copy. We'll want to test both.
[07:38] Ravi: we'll run both profiles: fp16 and 4-bit quant, measure p95 and quality regressions (we'll run your eval set). For streaming we also measure token latency and output hallucination rates on your evals.
[07:55] Aisha: one thing: our infra uses request multiplexing and we don't want token batching to re-order small sessions. Is that behavior preserved?
[08:03] Leah: Redwood's continuous batching is session-aware; we avoid cross-session re-ordering. There can be micro-batching within the same session to improve kernel utilization but we preserve ordering.
[08:17] Tom: do you support GPU topology where KV cache persists across requests to reduce recompute on the same host?
[08:25] Ravi: yes we have per-host KV cache with TTL and heuristics; if your session affinity hits the same host you see low-latency increments. We'll check your session distribution to estimate hit rates.
[08:40] Maya: security again - can we get audit logs for token-level traces? we cannot store PII.
[08:47] Leah: audit logs are configurable; we can redact PII at ingestion and provide structured logs with request IDs for observability. For Private deployments you can keep logs on-prem.
[08:59] Samir: pivoting to SLA mechanics - if we sign for Dedicated with a p95 SLA, how is that measured and credited?
[09:08] Ravi: SLA is measured over rolling windows for p95 on routed requests; credits are pro-rated based on missed windows and defined in the contract. We'll have legal draft language we can share.
[09:20] Maya: are there any limits on open connections for streaming? we may have long-lived websockets which tie resources.
[09:27] Leah: websocket streaming is supported; resource allocation counts concurrent streams for capacity planning. We recommend graceful idle timeouts and a keep-alive policy to reclaim stuck connections.
[09:41] Tom: in terms of observability, can we get per-token cost breakdown, per-route latency and token histograms?
[09:49] Ravi: yes Redwood Console shows token-level cost breakout, latency percentiles, per-model dashboards and tracing hooks to correlate with your logs.
[10:00] Maya: excellent. I'm a little nervous about hosted noisy neighbor - can you provide an example of a mitigation you've used?
[10:07] Leah: we've implemented smart routing, capacity tiers, and automatic fallback to lower-cost variants. For customers with hard SLOs we recommend reserved Dedicated pools.
[10:17] Aisha: what about failover across regions during a big burst? we need low-loss failover for streaming sessions.
[10:24] Ravi: cross-region failover is supported but streaming sessions will need reconnect semantics; we recommend sticky routing with multi-region warm standby in Dedicated for critical flows.
[10:38] Samir: ok let's walk the benchmark plan: Leah?
[10:42] Leah: plan is: 1) ingest anonymized traces 2) run replay against Hosted endpoint and Dedicated sandbox 3) test fp16 and 4-bit quant profiles, measure p95 and token emission jitter 4) provide cost per-token and recommendations (batching, cache TTLs) 5) share results and a short ops runbook. We'll also include a small failover test for region switch.
[11:06] Maya: sounds good. if possible can you show token inter-arrival CDFs? that's a big UX metric for us.
[11:13] Ravi: yes we'll include CDFs and jitter heatmaps.
[11:17] Tom: anything else on compliance we need to see?
[11:20] Leah: we'll attach SOC2 Type II cert, encryption-at-rest documentation and the Dedicated/Private deployment checklist.
[11:27] Maya: great. For cost modeling, can you include a scenario where we handle 250 concurrent during promo with 128-token avg?
[11:35] Samir: yes we'll run that as a stress scenario in the benchmark.
[11:39] Aisha: how do you instrument to ensure the bench itself doesn't overload the cluster and produce false positives?
[11:45] Ravi: our harness injects ramp and holds to let autoscaling stabilize; we capture backend utilization, queue depth and per-GPU metrics to separate client-side saturation vs infra induced latency.
[12:00] Tom: one final question - how long to provision Dedicated pool for a pilot? we want a 2-week pilot before committing.
[12:06] Leah: Dedicated pilot can be provisioned in 3-5 business days once we agree capacity. Private/on-prem takes longer.
[12:14] Maya: ok that's acceptable.
[12:17] Samir: wrapping up: recap next steps, Leah will own the benchmark and scripts, Ravi will run tests, I'll send pricing and SOC2 attachments. Maya to send traces and p95 per-flow. We aim to have run by Jan 25 and review deck by Feb 5.
[12:36] Maya: confirmed.
[12:38] Samir: anything else?
[12:41] Tom: no, thanks.
[12:43] Aisha: thanks everyone.
[12:46] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window.
